channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: A 1997 Washington Post review finds the Gilgamesh inside How Like a God
item.description: Joe Mayhew’s May 25, 1997 Washington Post review called Brenda W. Clough’s How Like a God “solid and even elegant.” The review reads Rob Lewis’s unwanted powers through the Gilgamesh epic and argues that the novel feels more like fantasy than conventional science fiction—a useful contemporary snapshot of the book’s reception.

item.title: FANAC preserves File 770’s December 1996 snapshot of fandom
item.description: FANAC’s File 770 archive includes issue 115 from December 1996, a 22-page scan supplied by Mark Olson. The issue offers a primary-source view of convention politics, awards, fan publishing and personalities at the end of that year—exactly the sort of searchable institutional memory that disappears when paper collections stay private.

item.title: National Archives opens a searchable trail through nine million WWII enlistment records
item.description: The National Archives explains how to search and download its electronic Army enlistment files covering 1938–1946. The database holds about nine million records, with fields such as serial number, birthplace, residence, occupation and enlistment date. Its limitations are important: it generally excludes officers and members of other service branches.

item.title: The 398th Bomb Group identifies the Black Widow crew and its final mission
item.description: The 398th Bomb Group Memorial Association pairs a crew photograph with the account of B-17G 43-37889, flown on its last mission by James Mitchell’s crew on Jan. 20, 1945. The page names the airmen, explains the crash near Mechtersheim and links the record to MACR 11797.

item.title: Cirsova Magazine closed to submissions after a decade-long run
item.description: Duotrope’s archived listing records Cirsova as permanently closed to submissions in September 2026. The page preserves its market profile—quarterly print publication, sword-and-planet and heroic fantasy focus, 2,000–7,500-word fiction range and semi-professional pay—making it a useful snapshot of the magazine’s final operating model.

item.title: Laminas XML-RPC 3.1.1 keeps a mature protocol current on PHP 8.5
item.description: The Oct. 9 release provides maintained XML-RPC client and server support for PHP 8.2 through 8.5, including value marshalling, faults and introspection. Packagist shows more than 2.6 million installs and 20 dependent packages, evidence that the protocol still has a practical modern footprint.

item.title: Grand Comics Database maps the complete Marvel Hostess ad run
item.description: The Grand Comics Database timeline turns Marvel’s 1975–81 Hostess ads into a browsable chronology, with issue-level credits and publication details. It is a practical reference for tracing the one-page adventures, checking disputed dates and identifying which comic books carried each snack-cake rescue.

item.title: St. Johns County Clerk opens a useful trail through public records
item.description: The clerk’s online-resources hub links court records, Official Records, commission documents and property-related filings in one place. For local-history or homeowners-association research, it is a direct route to recorded covenants, amendments, plats and meeting records without relying on secondary summaries.
item.source: St. Johns County Clerk of the Circuit Court and County Comptroller

item.title: Digital Comic Museum’s Fawcett archive makes Golden Age issues searchable
item.description: Digital Comic Museum gathers downloadable scans of public-domain Fawcett comics across Captain Marvel, western, humor and romance titles. The publisher index is especially useful for copyright archaeology because it exposes issue runs, dates and scan provenance while making hard-to-find material available for close comparison.

item.title: Copyright Office digitizes 25,238 historical record books
item.description: The newly completed collection holds more than 21.7 million images of applications and other records dating from 1870 to 1977. It offers a powerful new trail for researching ownership, registrations and copyright archaeology, with individual-record search planned for a future system update.

item.title: Reedsy relaunches Discovery as a paid review service for indie authors
item.description: Reedsy Discovery now offers a 350-word editorial review for $299, charged when a reviewer accepts the book, with delivery promised within 30 days. The Alliance of Independent Authors examines the service as a lower-cost rival to Kirkus while noting that Reedsy is an ALLi partner.

item.title: Kathleen Deagan surveys nearly a century of St. Augustine archaeology
item.description: For the St. Augustine Archaeological Association's 40th anniversary, archaeologist Kathleen Deagan traced the city's research tradition from the 1930s through 2026. The program highlights the people, excavations and public policies that made St. Augustine unusually strong in both professional and community archaeology.

item.title: The earlier St. Augustine Zero Milestone hides in plain sight
item.description: A public-history record documents the older coquina-sphere Zero Milestone for the Old Spanish Trail, including a photograph and its location near St. Augustine's visitor center. The modest marker is distinct from the taller 1928 monument and helps untangle the site's layered roadside history.

item.title: Brenda W. Clough's papers document a novelist's full working process
item.description: The University of Iowa's new finding aid covers 27 boxes of Brenda W. Clough manuscripts, proofs, research, maps, reviews, photographs and Worldcon correspondence. Drafts and supporting material trace books from initial handwriting through publication, while the collection's copyright terms distinguish research access from republication.

item.title: Java architects answer practical questions about the platform's direction
item.description: A recorded Devoxx session brings Java architects together for audience questions on virtual-thread scheduling, deprecations, modules, memory-layout inspection, primitive specialization, string templates, construction rules and automatic heap sizing. The show notes link directly to related talks for deeper follow-up.
